# Beyond this Guide {.unnumbered}

::: {.content-visible when-profile="stata"}
This guide is intended to provide a foundation and get you started in Stata. Beyond this foundation, there are many topics you might want to explore, depending on the nature of your studies. Below are some topics that might be of interest and some suggested resources for learning about them.

## Presenting results

Making nice (regression) tables: <https://repec.sowi.unibe.ch/stata/estout/esttab.html>

Coefficient plots: <https://repec.sowi.unibe.ch/stata/coefplot/getting-started.html>

Formatting options for graphs:

-   <https://stata.jeremiahdittmar.info/graphics/>

-   <https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/modules/graph8/gen-opts/>

Plotting interactions (moderation effects):

-   <https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/seminars/interactions-stata/>

-   <https://mattgolder.com/interactions>

## Data management

Subsetting data: <https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/modules/ubsetting-data/>

Labeling data: <https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/modules/labeling-data/>

Broad overview of data management topics: <https://stata.jeremiahdittmar.info/data-manipulation/>

Stata merging guide: <https://nathanfavero.com/wp-content/uploads/Stata_Merging_Guide.pdf>

Aggregating data: <https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/modules/collapsing-data-across-observations/>

More advanced programming concepts: <https://stata.jeremiahdittmar.info/advanced-programming/>

## Analysis

Overview of various statistical tests: <https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/other/mult-pkg/whatstat/>

Beyond ordinary linear regression: <https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/webbooks/reg/chapter4/regressionwith-statachapter-4-beyond-ols/>

Regression diagnostics: <https://sscc.wisc.edu/sscc/pubs/RegDiag-Stata/>

Binned scatterplots: <https://michaelstepner.com/binscatter/>
:::
